summary: Backend-only verification of Iteration 114 - task ownership audit fields (submitted_by_user_id/submitted_at, completed_by_user_id/completed_at, approved_by_user_id/approved_at) on esg_reporting_tasks. All 5 pytest scenarios PASS: (1) task_engine.generate_tasks_for_assignment initializes all 6 ownership fields to None on new tasks; (2) submitting a record without approval sets submitted_by=submitter, submitted_at, completed_by=submitter, completed_at, and leaves approved_by/approved_at None (approval_status=not_required); (3) submitting a record WITH approval required sets submitted_by/at only, keeps completed_by=None, completed_at=None, approved_by=None (approval_status=pending_approval); (4) approving the resulting approval request via POST /api/approval-workflows/requests/{id}/approve sets completed_by_user_id + completed_at + approved_by_user_id + approved_at all to the approver (approval_status=approved); (5) mutating task_assignees (simulated reassignment) preserves submitted_by_user_id / completed_by_user_id / completed_at on the task doc.
critical_code_review_comments: esg_records/service.py::_validate_user_assignment queries esg_assignments by top-level `assigned_to_user_id`, but AssignmentServiceV2.create_or_update_assignment (assignment_service_v2.py lines 366-398) does NOT write `assigned_to_user_id` on the assignment doc (only the assignees sub-collection has it). Consequence: for non-admin (or when allow_without_assignment=False) submitting via v2-created assignments, the assignment is not found and record creation is rejected. Admins survive because allow_without_assignment=True falls back to requires_approval=False - which silently loses the requires_approval flag from the real assignment. In the tests I had to backfill `assigned_to_user_id` via mongo to make the lookup work. Suggested fix: either (a) mirror assigned_to_user_id on the primary assignee onto the assignment doc, or (b) change _validate_user_assignment to also join with esg_assignment_assignees. This is a functional bug that will silently misclassify approval-required assignments as no-approval for admins.

approval_workflow/service.py::_process_approve writes completed_at and approved_at via two separate _now_iso() calls (lines 860 vs 862). Values may differ by a microsecond and store as different strings, complicating downstream equality checks. Compute once and reuse.

esg_records/service.py::_mark_task_completed only searches esg_reporting_tasks by category/period_key/subcategory/sub_subcategory/facility_id + assignee lookup. If the submitter is an admin who is NOT in esg_task_assignees and there is no legacy assigned_to_user_id match, the ownership fields are silently NOT written and no task is updated (early return line 888). Consider logging a warning instead of returning silently.

approval_workflow/service.py::_process_approve uses update_many on esg_reporting_tasks with a query that has no period_key when reporting_period is missing on the record - could accidentally mark completed_by/approved_by on unrelated tasks. Consider requiring period_key in the query and skipping the update if it can't be derived.
seed_data_creation: Each test: (a) creates a v2 esg_assignment via POST /api/esg-records/assignments with unique TEST_iter114_* subcategory, month-frequency, FY 2099-2100 to avoid collision; (b) patches assigned_to_user_id onto the assignment doc via mongo (see review comment); (c) submits an environment record via POST /api/esg-records/records/environment; (d) for the approve test, patches current_approvers via mongo and calls POST /api/approval-workflows/requests/{id}/approve. Cleanup deletes esg_reporting_tasks, esg_task_assignees, esg_assignments, esg_assignment_assignees, environment_records, approval_requests keyed by the created ids in a finally block.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file: /app/backend/tests/test_task_ownership_iter114.py. Uses pymongo + REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL + JWT admin login. Note the .env values MONGO_URL / DB_NAME contain literal double-quotes - strip('"') is applied. To reproduce silently-lost requires_approval bug: create a v2 assignment (no top-level assigned_to_user_id), do NOT patch mongo, then POST a record as a non-matching user - assignment lookup returns None and requires_approval defaults to False.
rca of the issue: N/A - all 5 target behaviours verified. However uncovered a related bug: AssignmentServiceV2 does not store `assigned_to_user_id` on the assignment doc while `_validate_user_assignment` filters on that field - causing silent requires_approval loss for admins. Documented in critical_code_review_comments.
